pageContent.heroExplanation: ARO is a democratic organisation of over 6,000 reclaimers. We fight for recognition, fair pay, and justice — because the people who recycle South Africa's waste deserve to be treated with dignity.
pageContent.aboutAroText: ARO is a mass-based democratic organisation of reclaimers, established in 2018. We call ourselves "reclaimers" — not "waste pickers" — because we are reclaiming both the recyclable materials that would otherwise go to landfill, and our dignity as workers doing essential work for South Africa. Our vision is a waste economy that recognises, includes, and fairly pays the reclaimers who already do most of the work. ARO Recycling operates alongside the organisation to put this vision into practice.
pageContent.historyText: Reclaimers began organising in 2016 in response to threats against their livelihoods, culminating in the first-ever march of Johannesburg's landfill and street reclaimers. That founding action grew into the mass-based movement that is ARO today.
pageContent.structuresText:
ARO is organised through 42 local branches across Johannesburg, each electing 2 representatives to sit on ARO's coordinating committee, which in turn elects an executive committee. ARO also has members organising in Mpumalanga and the Cape Town area.

pageContent.recyclingText: ARO Recycling is the trading arm connected to the organisation, helping put ARO's vision of reclaimer-led recycling into practice on the ground.
pageContent.reclaimersIntro: It is estimated that between 60,000 and 90,000 people work as informal reclaimers in South Africa. They collect the majority of used recyclables that are recycled in this country.
pageContent.whoAreReclaimersText: Reclaimers are the people who collect, sort, and sell recyclable materials from streets, depots, and landfills — work that keeps South Africa's cities clean and its recycling industry running, largely without recognition or fair pay.
pageContent.contributionsText: Reclaimers collect an estimated 80–90% of used recyclables that are recycled in South Africa (2015 estimate), saving municipalities hundreds of millions of rands in landfill costs every year while diverting waste that would otherwise pollute the environment.
pageContent.supportRecyclingText: Put out your recyclables in a way that reclaimers can access, or contact ARO to join the Recycling with Reclaimers programme in your area.
pageContent.supportSolidarityText: Businesses and organisations can partner with ARO, buy from reclaimers, and ensure recycling contracts support the people already doing the work.
pageContent.supportDonateText: Financial support helps ARO organise, campaign, and run programmes for reclaimers nationally. Contact us to find out how to donate.

campaigns.title: Separation at Source
campaigns.summary: ARO advocates for a model of Separation at Source that includes and pays reclaimers, rather than one that uses private companies to displace them.

campaigns.title: Membership
campaigns.summary: ARO organises reclaimers into a mass-based, democratic membership movement — building the collective power needed to win recognition, fair pay, and rights.

campaigns.title: Landfill Action Plans
campaigns.summary: According to Pikitup, all of Johannesburg's landfills will be full before the end of 2026 — putting thousands of reclaimers out of work and leaving the city drowning in its own waste. ARO's demand for social plans for landfill reclaimers solves both problems by providing reclaimer-led separation-at-source work that diverts waste from landfills.
campaigns.body:
According to Pikitup, all of the landfills in Johannesburg will be full before the end of 2026. This will put thousands of reclaimers out of work and leave the city drowning in its own waste. ARO's demand for social plans for landfill reclaimers can solve both of these problems by providing work for landfill reclaimers in reclaimer-led separation at source programmes that divert waste from landfills.

campaigns.title: Health
campaigns.summary: ARO campaigns for the health and safety of reclaimers, who face daily occupational hazards with little protection or support.

campaigns.title: COVID-19 Support
campaigns.summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, ARO organised emergency support for reclaimers who lost income when lockdowns halted their work.

campaigns.title: R50 Campaign
campaigns.summary: ARO's R50 Campaign mobilised reclaimers and allies around a concrete demand for fair payment for recyclable materials.

campaigns.title: Missing Persons Campaign
campaigns.summary: ARO campaigned to locate and support reclaimers who went missing while working, highlighting the dangers reclaimers face and the need for proper safety systems.

programmes.title: SAWPRS Registration & Service Fee Payment
programmes.summary: ARO is central to the development of the South African Waste Picker Registration System (SAWPRS), which grants reclaimers formal proof of occupation and connects them to service-fee payment from Producer Responsibility Organisations.

programmes.title: Mpumalanga Project
programmes.summary: ARO has expanded beyond Johannesburg to support reclaimers in Msukaligwa and Chief Albert Luthuli Local Municipalities in Mpumalanga — empowering them with knowledge, market connections, and formal registration.

policy.title: Waste Picker Integration Guideline
policy.summary: ARO was centrally involved in the stakeholder process that produced the 2020 DEFF Waste Picker Integration Guideline — the first national policy document to formally recognise reclaimers in South Africa's waste management system.

policy.title: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Regulations
policy.summary: ARO engages in EPR processes to ensure that reclaimers — who collect the majority of recyclable waste — receive a fair share of the service fees generated under Extended Producer Responsibility frameworks.

films.title: Reclaimers of Johannesburg
films.description: A documentary portrait of ARO members and their work across Johannesburg's streets and depots.

news.title: ARO Participates in Global Plastics Treaty Negotiations
news.body: ARO representatives joined waste picker organisations from across the Global South at the latest round of international negotiations toward a binding global plastics treaty. ARO's presence ensured that the voices of informal reclaimers — who handle the majority of plastic recycling — were heard in the drafting process.

news.title: SAWPRS Registration Expands to Mpumalanga
news.body: ARO's South African Waste Picker Registration System has extended its reach into Mpumalanga province, formally registering reclaimers in Msukaligwa and Chief Albert Luthuli municipalities for the first time. Registration grants reclaimers official proof of occupation and connects them to payment from Producer Responsibility Organisations.

reclaimers.name: Mantoa Khoali
reclaimers.quote: We do essential work. It is time this country paid us for it.
reclaimers.bio: Mantoa has been reclaiming in Johannesburg for over a decade. Her son completed agricultural college on her reclaimer income. She is ARO's Chairperson and one of the movement's most recognised organisers.
